Usage: klar contrast [options] <foreground> <background>

Calculate contrast between a foreground and a background. OKCA is polarity-aware
— argument order matters (some plugins are too).

Arguments:
  foreground            Foreground color (hex, rgb, oklch)
  background            Background color (hex, rgb, oklch)

Options:
  -t, --type <type>     Algorithm: okca, wcag2, deltaE (built-in), plus any
                        installed contrast-algorithm plugins (default: "okca")
  --gamut-map <method>  Out-of-gamut resolution: css (CSS Color 4 chroma
                        reduction), clip (clamp each channel into range), none
                        (measure the authored color; unavailable for algorithms
                        whose domain it exceeds) (default: "css")
  --allow-out-of-gamut  Exit 0 instead of 1 when an input is outside the gamut
                        (default: false)
  --json                Output as JSON (default: false)
  -q, --quiet           Print only the numeric value (default: false)
  -h, --help            display help for command

Out-of-gamut colors:
  A color authored in OKLCH can sit outside sRGB. It has to be resolved to a
  displayable color before it can be measured, so the reported number describes
  that mapped equivalent — not the color in your token file. That is a real
  answer to a different question, so it exits 1 rather than passing silently.
  Pass --allow-out-of-gamut to accept it, or read gamut.outOfGamut from --json.

  Reducing chroma is the fix, but the number will not move until the color is
  actually in gamut: chroma reduction maps every out-of-gamut chroma at a given
  lightness and hue onto the same boundary color.

  KLAR_GAMUT_MAP sets the default mapping process-wide. No environment
  variable waives the failure — that decision belongs at the call site.

Examples:
  $ klar contrast "#fff" "#000"
  $ klar contrast "#fff" "#000" --type wcag2
  $ klar contrast "oklch(50% 0.2 240)" "#000" -q
  $ klar contrast "oklch(0.79 0.22 25)" "#070e16" --json
  $ klar contrast "oklch(0.79 0.22 25)" "#070e16" --allow-out-of-gamut -q
  $ klar contrast "#fff" "#000" --type okca --json
Usage: klar find [options] <base-color> <reference-color>

Find a color that meets a target contrast by adjusting lightness

Arguments:
  base-color            Color to keep fixed
  reference-color       Color to adjust

Options:
  --target <n>          Target contrast value (required)
  -t, --type <type>     Algorithm: okca, wcag2, deltaE (built-in), plus any
                        installed contrast-algorithm plugins (default: "okca")
  --tolerance <n>       Acceptable overshoot above the target (never accepts
                        below it) (default: 0.5)
  --allow-desaturation  Permit reducing chroma to reach the target (default:
                        false)
  --json                Output as JSON (default: false)
  -q, --quiet           Print only the adjusted color hex (default: false)
  -h, --help            display help for command

By default only lightness moves. An out-of-gamut reference is first
chroma-reduced onto the gamut boundary — that is mandatory, since otherwise
there is no renderable color to return — but chroma is never traded for
contrast unless you ask.

When lightness runs out, the command exits 1 and reports what would solve it
under "resolvableBy", without applying it: trading brand saturation for
contrast is a design decision, not a computation. Pass --allow-desaturation
where that decision has already been made.

Branch on "reason", never on "message":
  ok                    target met
  lightness-exhausted   a solution exists but costs saturation — see resolvableBy
  chroma-exhausted      chroma reached 0 and the target is still unmet
  unreachable           no color meets this against this base; change the base

Examples:
  $ klar find "#ffffff" "#3b82f6" --target 4.5 --type okca
  $ klar find "#000" "#ccc" --target 4.5 --type wcag2
  $ klar find "#ffffff" "#3b82f6" --target 5.5 --json
  $ klar find "#070e16" "oklch(0.79 0.22 25)" --target 8 --allow-desaturation

  # Unreachable: this blue tops out at 5.9 on white, so this exits 1
  $ klar find "#ffffff" "#3b82f6" --target 7

content.text:
I ran every foreground in `tokens-system.json` against both backgrounds with `klar contrast` (OKCA, foreground on background, threshold 4.5). Then I used `klar find` to get a fix for each failing pair. `tokens-system.json` is unchanged.

**Results**

| Foreground | on `surface` #ffffff | on `surface-dark` #1a1a2e |
|---|---|---|
| text #1a1a2e | 15.8 ✅ | 1.0 (n/a) |
| inverse #ffffff | 1.0 (n/a) | 16.5 ✅ |
| muted #666666 | 4.8 ✅ | **2.4 ❌** |
| primary #3b82f6 | **2.9 ❌** | **1.9 ❌** |
| accent #e94560 | **2.8 ❌** | **2.0 ❌** |
| success #22c55e | **1.9 ❌** | **3.4 ❌** |

I treated `text` on dark and `inverse` on white as pairings that would never be used, since they are the same color as their background or its inverse. That is my assumption, so tell me if either should count.

**Fixes**

The fix keeps hue and changes lightness first. It reduces chroma (saturation) only when lightness alone can't reach 4.5. Those cases are marked "needs desaturation".

| Pair | Now | Proposed | OKCA | Change (ΔE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| primary on white | #3b82f6 (2.9) | **#115bcc** | 5.0 | 15, lightness only (L 0.65→0.50) |
| accent on white | #e94560 (2.8) | **#bf103f** | 4.7 | 13, lightness only |
| success on white | #22c55e (1.9) | **#047f38** | 4.6 | 22, needs desaturation (chroma 0.192→0.144) |
| muted on dark | #666666 (2.4) | **#919191** | 4.7 | 17, lightness only |
| success on dark | #22c55e (3.4) | **#41d870** | 4.8 | 5, lightness only |
| primary on dark | #3b82f6 (1.9) | **#7bacfc** | 4.5 | 13, needs desaturation (chroma 0.188→0.128) |
| accent on dark | #e94560 (2.0) | **#fe8a93** | 4.6 | 14, needs desaturation (chroma 0.199→0.141) |

- **One value per token won't work.** `primary`, `accent`, `success` and `muted` each need a darker value on white and a lighter one on dark. To fix both, split each into a light-surface and a dark-surface token, for example `primary` and `primary-on-dark`.
- **Two of the desaturation fixes are the largest changes:** `success` on white (ΔE 22) and `primary` on dark (ΔE 13). They visibly wash out the brand blue and green. I applied desaturation only because lightness alone can't reach 4.5 there.
- **`tokens.json` is separate.** The README calls it the source of truth, and it uses different, OKLCH-authored colors on white only. I didn't audit it. Some of its values, such as `success` at `oklch(0.7 0.3 150)`, look out of sRGB gamut, so it needs its own pass.

I can apply these to `tokens-system.json` or audit `tokens.json` next.

status_detail: 7 failing pairs found; awaiting decision on token structure
needs_action: confirm: split tokens into light/dark variants (primary + primary-on-dark, etc.), or use one value per token and accept the visual change?

The fix keeps hue and changes lightness first. It reduces chroma (saturation) only when lightness alone can't reach 4.5. Those cases are marked "needs desaturation".
